note: Gay (1955) described the soldier, the queen and the biology when publishing the new species; the original records the alate as 'Not known'. In the original the decimal point is printed as a colon (e.g. 0:66); it is restored here as a decimal point. This species lives in nests of Coptotermes.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale orange, paler in the dorsal median area, the head capsule occasionally tinged with light brown; basal third of the mandibles pale orange, the distal two-thirds pale rusty. Head almost with parallel sides, or the sides very slightly concave. Fontanelle distinct. Labrum slightly wider than long, obtusely conical, the hyaline tip usually with one distinct notch. Mandibles rather short and stout, about two-thirds the length of the head capsule, the middle generally retaining traces of teeth. Postclypeus markedly bilobed. Antennae short, extending only about one-fifth of their length beyond the mandibular tips, 13-segmented, segment 3 smallest. Pronotum about twice as wide as long, slightly narrower than the head, the anterior margin convex, the posterior margin shallowly concave. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Measurements (30 individuals, mm): body length 4.00—5.00; head length including mandibles 1.70—1.83; head length to the frontoclypeal suture 1.02—1.10; head width 0.66—0.77; pronotum length 0.31—0.35, width 0.60—0.69.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Alate unknown. Queen: head and thorax golden brown, the abdominal tergites slightly paler, the sternites, antennae and labrum pale yellowish brown; head, thorax and abdominal tergites and sternites densely covered with short hairs. Postclypeus longer than half its width, the anterior margin straight, the posterior margin strongly convex. Fontanelle lanceolate, with indications of extending forwards. Eyes medium-sized and projecting; ocelli oval, about half their long diameter from the eye. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 shortest and narrowest. Pronotum slightly wider than the head, slightly wider than long, the anterior margin wide and deeply concave, the sides first slightly rounded and then evenly narrowing to the shallowly concave posterior margin; the posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum wide and deeply concave. Tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Measurements (mm): head length to the tip of the labrum 1.06; head length to the frontoclypeal suture 0.55; head width 0.88; maximum eye diameter 0.28; ocellus length 0.09; pronotum length 0.82, width 0.93; body length 12.50; abdominal width 3.75. Biology: only two series of specimens are known, both collected from nests of Coptotermes brunneus; one series from cell groups within the clay walls outside the nest, the other from a separate nest body about one foot in diameter at the top of the nest containing the queen, reproductive nymphs, workers, soldiers and eggs; its nest consists of flat, clustered dark cells, with passages throughout the Coptotermes nest, often running parallel to the host passages but separated by thin walls. Distribution: Western Australia (51 and 66 miles north of Galena, October 1953 (month 10)). Distinction from A. hillii: the queen is smaller and much paler; the soldier is smaller, with a parallel-sided head, short antennae and relatively short, stout mandibles.
